text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Hungary presented its closing arguments Thursday and Friday at the International Court of Justice in the ongoing trial of the Gabcikovo hydropower plant dispute with Slovakia.

- Welfare Minister Mihaly Kokeny has ordered an investigation of the Health Authority and the Health Insurance Fund's supervision of the prescription and use of medicines and the Authority's asset management in 1996 and 1997.

- As part of President Arpad Goncz's visit, Foreign Ministry state secretary Istvan Szent-Ivanyi and his Mexican counterpart are to sign an agreement on abolishing visas in Mexico City today. On Friday, Ivan Niri, general manager of Eximbank said in Brazil that the bank concluded a $5 million credit agreement for the purchase of goods with Banco Unico.
- Four opposition parties as well as farmers' groups criticised the cabinet's national agriculture programme, finding its basic principles unsuitable for debate.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn on Friday pledged to increase state subsdies to agriculture in accordance with the rise in the GDP. (Sat.)
- Socialist Party caucus leader Imre Szekeres said that his party must run for the elections on its own.
- The Left-wing Group within the Socialist Party criticised the present party leadership on Saturday.
- Young Democrat president Viktor Orban said a large number of non-party people and former Christian Democrats have joined his party.
- Smallholders president Jozsef Torgyan said on Saturday that the signs of a general crisis are apparent in all walks of life in Hungary.
- Romania will be the sixth CEFTA member from July 1.
- Consumer prices rose 1.9 percent in March.
- The Central European Bank Ltd recorded an after-tax profit of HUF 9.3 billion in 1996 and will pay a 32.5 percent dividend.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- Austrian Interior Minister Karl Schlogl noted that the open border has created new problems and resulted in a tremendous immigration wave through Hungary, the Czech Republic and Slovakia, and "we must stop that".
- A Slovak Foreign Ministry official warned that if his country is not invited to NATO in July, it could destabilise Central Europe and render relations with neighbouring countries tense.
- Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said on Friday he is ready to meet Hungarian Premier Gyula Horn.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The increase in industrial production continued in February when the output went up 2.4 percent.
- Sales in the light industry sector are likely to stagnate or decrease further this year, said a Ministry of Industry official.
- The share of the black economy is nowhere near the 30 percent that some claim, said Istvan Janos Toth of the economic research firm Kopint-Datorg.
- One of the EBRD's main objectives in Hungary is to support companies wishing to list on the stock exchange. The other priority is financing infrastructure investments.

- Takarekbank Rt and 231 cooperative savings banks belonging to it will be transformed into a group offering comprehensive banking services, Friedbert Malt of Deutsche Genossenschaftsbank said on Friday. (Sat.)
